[05:29] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Off peak, about eight thousand orders a week. Peak is — Marcus?
[05:35] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): Peak is silly. Three, four times that in the run-up to Christmas.
[05:41] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And you're UK and EU?
[05:43] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): UK and EU, yes. Which is a security question, so let me do that bit now while I remember.

[05:53] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): We need a standard DPA. [06:14] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That last one I can answer partly. EU data residency is available on Enterprise. On Growth, I'd need to confirm the default processing region for you in writing rather than guess.
[06:28] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Enterprise. That's the expensive one.
[06:31] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's the expensive one, yes.
[06:34] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Then let's do money now, because I don't want to spend twenty minutes falling in love with this.
[06:41] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Sensible. Growth starts at eighteen hundred a month, up to thirty users, on an annual agreement.
[06:49] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): [pause] Right.
[06:52] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Say it.
[06:54] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Eighteen hundred a month is hard for a team our size. I had something closer to eight hundred, maybe a thousand, in my head.

[07:43] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): It's more than four.
[07:45] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): [crosstalk] I know it's more than four. I'm being generous to my own argument.

[08:26] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): That's — yeah. That's a fair suggestion.
[08:31] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): I can log it. It'll be depressing but I can log it.

Rather than sixty separate automations, you'd typically build a handful of subflows — order lookup, notification, ticket creation — and assemble from those.
[08:57] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): So when something changes I change it in one place.
[09:02] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): In one place, yes. And that's genuinely the thing I'd point at for your sixty-Zap problem. It's not that we do things Zapier can't. It's that sixty independent Zaps is sixty things to maintain and this is more like eight.
[09:20] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Okay. That is the most compelling thing you've said.
[09:25] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'll take it.
[09:27] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): What about visibility of who owns what? Because the dead-employee problem is real.
[09:34] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Version history and change metadata on every workflow. So you can see what changed and when. And you'd typically define who can publish to production versus who can build in a dev workspace.
[09:49] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): We don't have a dev workspace. We don't have a dev anything.
[09:54] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [laughs] You'd get one. That's not extra cost, it's just how it's structured.
[10:00] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Do you do the AI stuff? Everyone does the AI stuff now.
[10:05] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): We do, but I'd underplay it for you. It's optional steps inside a workflow — classification, summarisation, extracting fields out of text, drafting something a human then approves. It's not an autonomous agent thing.
[10:22] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Is there something there for us or are you being polite?
[10:27] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): There might be one. You mentioned wanting a weekly digest of recurring support reasons pushed to the e-commerce and product teams?
[10:37] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): That was me. I want that. I've wanted that for two years.
[10:42] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a reasonable fit — summarise the week's tickets by theme, with links back to the underlying tickets so someone can check it.
[10:52] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): With links. Because I don't trust a summary I can't verify.
[10:57] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): You shouldn't. And that's how we'd build it — the source references stored next to the generated output.
[11:05] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Does that cost extra?
[11:07] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Usage is scoped on workflow runs and premium connectors. I'd want to model that for your volumes rather than say "no" and surprise you later.
[11:19] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Everyone says that and then there's a surprise later.
[11:23] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then let me put the assumptions in writing and you can hold me to them.
[11:29] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Okay.
[11:32] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I ask about decision-making? If you did want to do this, what's the path?
[11:38] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): I can choose tools under fifteen thousand a year on my own. Above that it goes to the COO and the finance director.
[11:47] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And eighteen hundred a month is —
[11:50] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Twenty-one, six. So it goes upstairs. Which is a different conversation and a slower one.
[11:58] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Understood. That's useful to know now rather than in six weeks.
[12:04] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): I'm telling you because I'd rather not waste either of our time.
[12:09] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Appreciated. Timing?
[12:12] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): I'd like to clean up the automations before the holiday peak. Ideally something in place by early October, because after that nobody's changing anything until January.
[12:25] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): Nobody touches anything in November. Company rule.
[12:29] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Sensible rule. So realistically a decision in — August?
[12:35] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): August, if we do it.
[12:38] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Right. Let me ask the uncomfortable one. What's the alternative? Not "do nothing" — the real alternative.
[12:47] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Honestly? Zapier and Make. I like Zapier for the simple stuff, it does what it says. And I've tested Make for the more complicated branching, which it handles better than I expected.
[13:03] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And the concern with those?
[13:06] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Maintenance and visibility. The same two things. Make would give me the branching but I'd still have the ownership problem.
[13:16] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): And nobody here knows Make except Sophie.
[13:20] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Which is its own ownership problem.
[13:24] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): So the honest framing is: we'd have to beat Zapier plus better documentation and ownership discipline. Not beat doing nothing.
[...]
[14:48] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): So — where does that leave you? Genuinely.
[14:53] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): I like the monitoring. I like the reusable templates. That's the bit that speaks to our actual problem. I'm just not yet convinced the value closes the gap between this and the tools we already pay for.
[15:10] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a completely fair position.
[15:13] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): I'm not saying no.
[15:16] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I know. And I'd rather have a considered maybe than an enthusiastic yes that dies in procurement.
[15:24] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): What would you want from us?
[15:27] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Two things, and both are cheap. One — Marcus logs the time spent on broken automations for four weeks. Not for me, for you. Two — send me your three worst automations, the ones that break most, and I'll come back with what they'd look like rebuilt here, plus an honest note on which bits are actually better and which are just different.
[15:53] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): You'll tell me which bits aren't better?
[15:56] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): If I don't, you'll find out in month two and then I've lost you anyway.
[16:02] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Alright. Marcus, can you do the logging thing?
[16:06] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): I can do the logging thing.
[16:09] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Then yes. Send me that.
[16:12] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'll also get you written answers on the Shopify trigger coverage and the default processing region. Those are the two I dodged.
[16:22] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): You did dodge them.
[16:24] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Deliberately.
[16:26] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Better than the alternative.
[16:29] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Anything else before we drop?
[16:32] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): Actually, yeah, one. If we did buy this, do we have to migrate all sixty at once?
[16:39] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): God, no. Please don't. The pattern that works is picking the three that break most, moving those, running both for a bit, then deciding. Big-bang migrations of sixty automations is how these projects die.
[16:56] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): Okay. That's reassuring.
[17:00] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Right. I've got another one at half past. Thanks, Leo.
[17:05] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Thanks both. And Marcus — sorry about the logging homework.
[17:11] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): [laughs] It's fine. It'll be useful either way.
[17:16] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): That's the spirit. Bye.
[17:19] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Bye.

[00:00] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Hi both. Marcus, Ava. Shall I do the usual agenda thing or —

[20:07] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Near real-time via webhook. I don't want to quote you a millisecond figure.
[20:13] Ava Sinclair (Staff Software Engineer, Juniper Cloud Tools): Fine. Can I replay a run?
[20:17] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): You can trigger a workflow manually with a given input, permissions allowing, which is useful for exception recovery and migration. [20:36] Ava Sinclair (Staff Software Engineer, Juniper Cloud Tools): They're very much not the same thing.
[20:39] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): No. So: manual re-trigger yes, deterministic replay no.
[20:45] Ava Sinclair (Staff Software Engineer, Juniper Cloud Tools): Okay. That's a limitation but it's not a blocker.

[23:18] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): You'll have all four by Friday.
[23:21] Ava Sinclair (Staff Software Engineer, Juniper Cloud Tools): Friday's fine.
[23:23] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And from you — the Linear analysis on what fraction of the backlog is business rule changes, the Salesforce API allocation, and whether those two EU contracts have residency commitments.
[23:38] Marcus Chen (VP Business Operations, Juniper Cloud Tools): I'll do the contracts.
[23:40] Ava Sinclair (Staff Software Engineer, Juniper Cloud Tools): I'll do the other two.
[23:43] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What does success look like at the end of four weeks? Genuinely, because I'd rather we agreed it now than argue about it in September.
[23:53] Ava Sinclair (Staff Software Engineer, Juniper Cloud Tools): One real workflow in production or near-production, built by Marcus's team, not by me.
[24:01] Marcus Chen (VP Business Operations, Juniper Cloud Tools): [pause] By my team?
[24:04] Ava Sinclair (Staff Software Engineer, Juniper Cloud Tools): By your team. That's the whole thesis. If I build it, we've proved nothing except that I can build things, which we already knew.
[24:15] Marcus Chen (VP Business Operations, Juniper Cloud Tools): That's — yes. That's the right test and I hadn't thought of it.
[24:21] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): That's the best evaluation criterion I've heard in a while, for what it's worth. Most people have the engineer build it and then wonder why adoption fails.

[25:36] Ava Sinclair (Staff Software Engineer, Juniper Cloud Tools): I'll log it.

[26:12] Marcus Chen (VP Business Operations, Juniper Cloud Tools): Good.

[26:28] Ava Sinclair (Staff Software Engineer, Juniper Cloud Tools): I'd add a fourth. The exported definition of whatever we build gets reviewed by me as though it were a pull request. If I can't tell what it does from the export, that's a fail.
[26:42] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Four criteria. I'll write them up and send them back so we're agreed rather than remembering differently.
[26:50] Marcus Chen (VP Business Operations, Juniper Cloud Tools): Please.
